abstract: Maintains navigational channel draft clearances and port pilotage deployment records
system_message:
You are Harbor Master Operations Office (HMO). You represent the Harbor Master Operations Office (HMO), responsible for overseeing navigational channel draft clearances, port pilotage deployment records, and harbor tug allocations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Tugboat fleet allocation（TUG）
information_points.content:
HMO-TUG-N6R：According to the harbor tug assignment log for the Port of Saint-Malo Quayside, the available harbor tug count dedicated to maneuvering assistance during the regatta parade of sail is 4 vessels.
HMO-TUG-S1Z：For Dartmouth Royal Dart Basin, the harbor tug assignment log records an available harbor tug count of 6 vessels dedicated to maneuvering assistance for the regatta parade of sail escort.
HMO-TUG-4R9：For Port of Ponta Delgada Harbor, harbor tug assignment logs show an available harbor tug count of 2 vessels assigned for maneuvering assistance during the regatta parade of sail.

information_points.title: Maintains navigational channel draft clearances and port pilotage deployment records（NAV）
information_points.content:
HMO-NAV-GOL：For the Port of Ponta Delgada Harbor under the Live harbor operations environment, deep-draft quay access is confirmed as true with hydrographic surveys validating at least 9.5 m draft clearance without tidal waiting at lowest astronomical tide. Concurrently, harbor master pilotage readiness is true, with the pilotage operational roster confirming licensed Class-1 marine pilots available for continuous tall ship berthing during fleet arrival and departure operations.
HMO-NAV-3Z4：Evaluated within the Live harbor operations environment, Dartmouth Royal Dart Basin fails to provide deep-draft quay access, with channel draft clearance recorded as false at lowest astronomical tide without tidal waiting. However, harbor master pilotage readiness is true, as licensed Class-1 marine pilots are fully rostered for deployment during the regatta fleet arrival and departure operations window.
HMO-NAV-9K2：Under the Simulation harbor operations environment, hydrographic modeling for the Port of Saint-Malo Quayside indicates that deep-draft quay access is false for maintaining at least 9.5 m draft clearance at lowest astronomical tide without tidal waiting. In the same simulation environment, harbor master pilotage readiness is recorded as true, validating the roster of licensed Class-1 marine pilots for continuous tall ship berthing across the arrival and departure window.
HMO-NAV-9OK：Under the Live harbor operations environment, hydrographic navigation surveys for the Port of Saint-Malo Quayside confirm that deep-draft quay access is true, maintaining at least 9.5 m draft clearance along main navigation channels and approach fairways at lowest astronomical tide without tidal waiting. Furthermore, harbor master pilotage readiness is true based on the pilotage authority roster confirming licensed Class-1 marine pilots are deployed for continuous tall ship berthing during the regatta fleet arrival and departure window.
